relevance_note: A case report of a consanguineous family with a homozygous LPIN2 variant: "revealed a homozygous G > A transition in LPIN2 (c.G2207A)".
method_note: Hand-built from a full reading of this short letter; a Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Six in-scope people: the index child ('patient'; role words only, no own label; sex not stated), mother, elder sister, two younger brothers (labelled 'brother of patient' and 'brother of patient 2', in order of mention) and father. Contradiction: the text gives the variant as c.G2207A, while the Fig. 1 legend gives 'c.2208 G > A' (also 'LPIN2 c.2208' for the pedigree); the text string is recorded. Contradiction: the father is described as 'asymptomatic apart from non-specific knee pains' in the text but as having 'manifested no clinical symptoms' in the Fig. 1 legend; the knee-pain row is kept and checklist 'joint pain' is left not reported for him. Variant rows exist for the patient, mother, father and both brothers (text: two brothers, mother and father homozygous); the elder sister's genotype is not stated in text (only shown in the pedigree figure, not available), so she has no variant row. Inheritance left 'not reported' for the patient and brothers: both parents are stated to be homozygous carriers and the enum has no biparental value; the statement is in parental_testing_statement. PolyPhen2 prediction and gnomAD frequency were not recorded as functional evidence (in silico, not an assay). 'No evidence of skin involvement' is stated for 'one consanguineous family' and applied to all six family members as a group statement (excluding neutrophilic dermatosis). 'An extensive immunology/infectious diseases workup was inconclusive or normal' excludes nothing specific and was not recorded. Checklist CRMO marked observed for the patient from multiple MRI osteitis lesions and new lesions; for the brothers ('confirmed osteitis by MRI' only) it is left not reported. Disease label 'Majeed syndrome' recorded only for the patient (legend 'Family affected by Majeed syndrome'); left not reported for relatives. Mother's and sister's 'milder forms of anaemia' not marked microcytic; 'limb pains' not mapped to bone or joint pain. n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no count.

treatment_summary.value: NSAIDs and infrequent oral corticosteroids (partial transient response); at age 6, bisphosphonates (3 monthly intravenous pamidronate) with transient improvement; then daily subcutaneous anakinra (1 mg/kg) with resolution of bone pain and normalization of inflammatory markers
span: Initial management for mild intermittent osteitis involved NSAIDs and infrequent oral corticosteroids to which there was partial transient response
At the age of 6, due to ongoing symptomatic osteitis (Fig. 1D), a therapeutic trial of bisphosphonates (3 monthly intravenous pamidronate) as for sporadic CNO was initiated
IL-1 blockade with daily subcutaneous anakinra (1 mg/kg) was commenced
This resulted in resolution of bone pain, significant improvement of bone lesions on MRI scan, normalization of inflammatory markers

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: clinical features indicative of possible Majeed syndrome, then genetic testing on the Oxford Red Cell Panel revealing a homozygous LPIN2 variant
span: a conglomeration of features indicative of possible Majeed syndrome
The proband’s DNA was screened using the Oxford Red Cell Panel [5]
including LPIN2, which revealed a homozygous G > A transition in LPIN2 (c.G2207A)
